chapter: Mambo, the Palladium and Cubop City
title: The competitive hit year of 1949
summary: Asked about the many mambo hits of 1949, Machito says other bands' success was good for the music and rivalry is egotism.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: I see, okay. Thus, the mambo officially kicked off. Thus, in 1949 the mambo began after the popularity of "Mambo No. 5", by Perez Prado. There are a lot of good recordings I ahh - "Asia Minor", "El Mambo de Broadway" - Alfredito Valdes - Tito Puente's "Abaniquito", Damiron & Chapousaux's "Anabacoa"; it was a great year for music. When all these records were being heard in El Barrio, ahh "110th St. and 5th Ave.", by Noro and Ponce, were out at the same time, did it occur to you that the music industry was getting very competitive - because here you had all these hits at one time- Were you aware of it?

Well, to us it was good for the music because you just can't have everything. Selfishness or egotism is for people that they don't like what they practice. Is like a good doctor, another doctor comes up with some ideas about an operation or an injection or whatever, and get jealous about the other guy that when he finishes his practice he goes to his house and plays with his children or read the paper, watch baseball or boxing. You have to accept that the other person spends the leisure time in something for humans so .....
